deep.reconstruction:
This page opens a new section of the 1983 Teichmüller notes. The heading reads "Courbes exceptionnelles de type (1,1) (sur C)", meaning genus-1 curves with one marked point whose automorphism group is larger than ±1. These are the two orbifold points of M_{1,1}: j=1728 (the square lattice Z[i]) and j=0 (the hexagonal lattice Z[ρ]). Part A treats the square case.

(1) The groupoid of elliptic curves isomorphic to El_0 := C/Z[i] is equivalent to the classifying groupoid B(Aut El_0).
- Here Aut El_0 = μ_4(C) = Z[i]^× ≅ Z/4Z.
- So this groupoid is equivalent to the groupoid of μ_4-torsors.
- Grothendieck calls these "oriented combinatorial squares": a cyclically ordered set of 4 vertices with Z/4 acting by rotation.
- The equivalence sends E to Isom(El_0, E). The inverse is the twist El_0(S) = El_0 ∧^{Z/4} S, the contracted product.

(2) Geometric version of the inverse functor.
- Realize S canonically as a Euclidean square in a Euclidean plane V_S, with centre o.
- The two diagonals give coordinate axes up to sign.
- These axes determine a lattice Γ_S, a discrete subgroup of rank 2 (the transcription's "non discret" is a misreading).
- Then El_0(S) ≅ X_S = V_S/Γ_S.
- The marginal sketches show the lattice Z[i] with ±1, ±i, and the tilted square tiling the plane by translates.

(3) 2-torsion of X_S.
- There is a canonical point of order 2, η_S, corresponding to (1+i)/2. It is fixed by multiplication by i, since i(1+i)/2 ≡ (1+i)/2 mod Z[i].
- The other two points of order 2 (1/2 and i/2) are exchanged by the generator i of μ_4 ≅ Aut(X_S).
- The final line, an N.B. on how η_S can be defined, is cut off.

Purpose: an explicit, combinatorial (dessin-like) description of the exceptional points of M_{1,1}. This fits the 1983 programme of describing Teichmüller groupoids and the Galois-Teichmüller tower in terms of combinatorial data (maps, oriented squares and, presumably next, hexagons).
errors: Terminology: classically the j=1728 (square) curve is called 'harmonique' (cross-ratio −1), while 'équianharmonique' designates j=0 (hexagonal). 'Anharmonique de type carré' is a nonstandard or loose label.

Minor: the precise construction of Γ_S from the square (vertices vs. diagonal axes, scaling) is only sketched. Any normalization gives a lattice homothetic to Z[i], so this is harmless up to isomorphism.

ideas.what: Groupoid of elliptic curves with CM by Z[i] (j=1728) equivalent to groupoid of μ_4-torsors ('oriented combinatorial squares'); curves obtained by twisting C/Z[i]
ideas.modern_name: Residual gerbe B(μ_4) at the orbifold point j=1728 of the moduli stack M_{1,1}; twisted forms via contracted product
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Deligne–Mumford stack theory; Serre/Grothendieck twisting by torsors)
ideas.where_published: Twisting by torsors is general Grothendieck theory (SGA/Giraud). The exceptional points of M_{1,1} are mentioned in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) in the context of the Teichmüller tower.

ideas.what: Canonical realization of the twisted curve as V_S/Γ_S, where V_S is the Euclidean plane spanned by the square and Γ_S is the lattice from its diagonals
ideas.modern_name: Square tiling / regular map {4,4} on the torus; dessin d'enfant picture of j=1728
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein); dessins-type viewpoint popularized after Esquisse

ideas.what: Canonical 2-torsion point (1+i)/2 fixed by Aut; the other two 2-torsion points swapped by i
ideas.modern_name: Action of CM automorphism on E[2] for j=1728

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but standard description of the j=1728 point of M_{1,1} as the gerbe B(μ_4), with a combinatorial-Euclidean realization. It is consistent with the Esquisse viewpoint and contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: '(sous-groupe non discret de rang 2)' should read '(sous-groupe discret de rang 2)'.
The heading insertion 'exceptionnelles' modifies 'Courbes', i.e. 'Courbes exceptionnelles de type (1,1)'; 'ell.' is inserted before 'anharmonique'.
The parenthetical describing η_S ('classe par entiers glissés') is uncertain. It plausibly refers to the centres of the translated squares, i.e. the point (1+i)/2.
'CNB' is likely 'N.B.'; the final clause is truncated.
